description:

=== THE STALE PREMISE: THIS ROW'S DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG, AND SO WAS THE ARCHITECT'S CORRECTION OF IT ===
Layer 1, the row description's claim -- "Resources is FROZEN with a SOON chip (apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/shell-model.ts:111)". CONFIRMED FALSE at HEAD, same as the architect measured: `grep -n SOON apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/shell-model.ts` -> exit 1, ZERO hits. Line 110 is the `resources` NAV_ENTRIES entry, `{ id: "resources", label: "Resources", icon: "M12 3.5 20.5 12 ..." }` -- an id, a label and an SVG path, no state at all.

Layer 2, step-2's own correction -- "the real mechanism is the per-entry `live: boolean` flag declared at shell-model.ts:25, with nav-rail.tsx:112-124 rendering the chip". THE FIRST HALF IS ALSO FALSE, and child 1's worker found the same thing independently. Measured: shell-model.ts:25 `readonly live: boolean;` is a member of `interface ConnectionDescriptor` (declared :21), whose siblings are key/label/toneVar/actionsEnabled/staleLabel/banner and whose five instances at :39/:43/:48/:53/:67 are the relay CONNECTION states -- it drives the sparkline animation, not the nav. NAV_ENTRIES carries no `live` field on any of its six entries; `grep 'live:' shell-model.ts` returns only those five connection rows. A worker chasing `live` on a nav entry would have found nothing to flip.

Layer 3, WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. The freeze is a ROUTE, not a flag. `BUILT_NAV_ROUTES` (shell-routes.ts:88, `Partial<Readonly<Record<NavId, CordumRoute>>>`) lists the destinations the build implements; `resolveNavDestinations()` (:97-105) maps NAV_IDS over it and emits `{ id, reason: "NAV_DESTINATION_NOT_BUILT", route: null }` for any id ABSENT from the map. nav-rail.tsx then derives `unavailable = reason !== null` (:80) and renders, on that one boolean, the disabled button (:88), `data-unavailable-reason` (:87), `aria-describedby` (:85) and the SOON StatusChip with testid `cr.nav.<id>.unavailable` (:118-124). Child 1 lifted the freeze by adding `resources: Object.freeze({ kind: "resources" })` at shell-routes.ts:93 -- confirmed present at HEAD -- plus the route kind and its union arm. nav-rail.tsx was NOT edited: the chip machinery and the reason vocabulary are intact and still fire for any future unbuilt id.

Layer 2's SECOND half was right and is the part that matters for grading: the observable is the RENDERED marker. QA grades DoD 1 on `queryByTestId("cr.nav.resources.unavailable")` being null, the button not disabled, and no data-unavailable-reason -- never on a source grep for a string that was never in that file. The only asserter of that testid at HEAD is apps/control-room/src/v2/cordum-app.test.tsx.

=== A CONSEQUENCE NEITHER THE ROW NOR THE PLAN ANTICIPATED, worth carrying to QA ===
NAV_IDS has exactly six members and BUILT_NAV_ROUTES now maps all six (approvals, goals, runs, policy, health, resources). So at HEAD the `NAV_DESTINATION_NOT_BUILT` branch of resolveNavDestinations() is UNREACHABLE from production data -- `resources` was the last unbuilt destination. Any test that filters resolveNavDestinations() for `reason !== null` now iterates an EMPTY list and passes vacuously. Child 1's QA caught exactly this (three such arms, two in cordum-shell-responsive.test.tsx, none named by that child's plan) and fixed it with an injected all-unbuilt roster plus set-equality against NAV_IDS, replacing a count pair. That is the shape of global rail 9 in miniature and it is already discharged; recording it so nobody re-opens it as a gap.

implementationPlan.note:
THE ROSTER BITES. Verified by BREAKING it four ways, not by reading its assertions. Full transcript in comment-f3eaf818; this note is the verdict per sub-clause.

(a) THE SERVED SET IS DERIVED, NOT HAND-KEPT -- CONFIRMED by reading the test. Three independent extractors run over the DISPATCH FILE'S OWN SOURCE TEXT: `rosterIdentifiers()` takes the identifiers inside the `JSON_ROUTES` array literal, `branchIdentifiers()` regexes `path === ([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)` over the chain AFTER `const body = await readBoundedBody`, `guardIdentifiers()` takes the `path === X && request.method` guards. The served set is `branches UNION {DOCUMENT_DOSSIER_PATH}` -- the one member the chain's unconditional trailing `else` serves -- compared to the roster with `toStrictEqual`, i.e. SET EQUALITY, so both failure directions bite: a roster entry with no branch (404 by fallthrough) and a branch with no roster entry (never reached). The union is not a loophole: the test pins `expect(source).toContain("} else serveDocumentDossier(response, request, options, body);")` and `expect(branches.has("DOCUMENT_DOSSIER_PATH")).toBe(false)`, so turning that else into an `else if` reds. There is no third hand-kept copy anywhere in the chain. It identifies by IDENTIFIER rather than value, which is the right call in a file that would otherwise need 25 imports re-resolved, and the file cannot drift from itself. A positive-control arm floors every scan (>20 roster, >20 branches, >15 guards, >25 proxied, >100 files walked, >15 paths) so no arm can pass by comparing two empty sets.

(b) BOTH DIRECTIONS, VERIFIED BY DOING. Baseline and final state both Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 14 passed (14) EXIT 0.
  - DELETE A CONSUMER (drill 1): mutated the route literal in live-product-contract-gate-1.ts:22. 1 failed | 13 passed, exactly the consumption arm, `+ "/product-contract/gate-1/read"`.
  - ADD A SERVED ROUTE WITH NO CONSUMER (drill 2): wired a complete new registration -- constant, roster entry, non-POST guard, dispatch branch, dev-proxy pin -- so the consumption direction was the only one left exposed. 2 failed | 12 passed: the consumption arm reddened with `+ "/parent-drill/read"` as intended, and SEPARATELY `expect(roster.size).toBe(30)` reddened `expected 31 to be 30` while the set-equality half of that same arm correctly passed.
  THAT SECOND RED IS A REAL FINDING AND I WOULD NOT HAVE SEEN IT BY READING. `.toBe(30)` at :313 is a frozen roster count -- exactly what epic rail 3 forbids -- and it is redundant with the `toBeGreaterThan(20)` floor the positive control already asserts. Every future row that lands a read route will red this arm for reasons unrelated to its own work. Routed to the epic-final hardening row.

(c) EXCLUSIONS CARRY REASONS, AND THE REASONS ARE LOAD-BEARING. All eleven DoD-named exclusions have a stated SENSE in `KIND_EXCLUSION_SENSE`, each pinned THREE ways in one loop: the prose must contain the literal `<kind>: <SENSE>`, the kind must be in GENERATED_COMMAND_BUILDERS, and its presence in PAYLOAD_KEYS must match `sense.startsWith("ADVERTISED_AND_SERVED")`. planning.write is handled as NOT_A_COMMAND_KIND and asserted absent from both seams while equal to CAPABILITIES.PLANNING. cutover.* and work.* are expanded FROM the advertised seam by prefix, not from a glob, so a new cutover kind lands in a set-equality diff. DRILLED (drill 3): deleting graph.supersede's three prose lines while leaving its map entry reds "states a sense per DoD-named exclusion", `expected ... to contain 'graph.supersede: ADVERTISED_AND_SERVE...'`. A sense cannot be added without writing its reason.

(d) REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PATH IS CONSUMED, AND NOT BY SPECIAL-CASING -- the specific failure mode the plan's risk section named. It appears in NEITHER census. Whole-tree census: five of its seven control-room mentions are COMMENTS, which `stripComments` erases before the walk sees them, leaving exactly two real consumers -- live-repository-remote.ts:17 and a literal `fetch("/repository/remote/read", ...)` at live-publication-candidate.ts:20. Drill 4 mutated BOTH: 1 failed | 13 passed, `+ "/repository/remote/read"`. So the plan-time gap (comment-81312c74 on task-19d2329c) was genuinely closed by task-e6000b57 through real call sites, and the roster would name it again the moment they went. The roster is NOT red here, and that is the correct result rather than a bought one.
